lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: perimeter, area, and shape classification in the completed design
lessonRef.title: Transfer, reflection, and publication: perimeter, area, and shape classification in the completed design

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different setting than the problems below.

items.prompt: Which quadrilateral has four equal sides and four right angles?

steps: Four equal sides and four right angles describes a square.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A rectangular field is 14 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
Which quadrilateral is defined by having four equal sides, but not necessarily right angles?
A rectangular field is 11 in long and 14 in wide. What is its perimeter?
Which quadrilateral is defined by having exactly one pair of parallel sides?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.

items.prompt: A rectangular field is 11 cm long and 8 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Which quadrilateral is defined by having four right angles, with opposite sides equal?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
